title: The Most Boring Box in the World

bands.1:
You have won Slick Vinnie's badge. Now he is on your side.

"You never bought a thing from me, Captain," he says. "The Vantamart gets a delivery at nine. Tonight, the delivery is you."

Indi makes the disguises. Everyone hides in a box that says, "LIFE-SIZED MAXX PILLOW."

Gus holds up a grey ball. "The Belly-Button Fluff Bomb! Two years of my own fluff. That's not gross. That's science."

At nine, Vinnie pushes the boxes to the back door.

"Fresh stock!" he tells the Goldies. "Everyone is ordering these! Sign here!"

"Why is that box breathing?" asks a Goldie.

"Deluxe model," says Vinnie.

You are in! The warehouse is full of gold hoodies and Maxx pillows.

At the back are tiny cages. The sign says, "LIVE MERCH." Inside are Bilbolsters and Proovils in tiny gold hoodies. They are models for Maxx's photos. Wren opens the cages.

Next is an office. Zed types IAMPRICELESS. The door opens.

Wren goes straight to a grey box. It says, "BORING STUFF. DO NOT OPEN."

"He hides the important things in boring boxes," she says. "Lucky guess."

Inside is the Rescue Fund book.

Tully reads it. "Money in: four million dollars. Money for Creatures: one carrot. Money for a second gold jet ski: all the rest!"

"Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!" laughs Spruikoo.

You put the book in your jacket. That is the proof.

Then the lights flash on. Goldies run in!

"The Reef Rays scored!" whispers Tully. "They're only losing by sixty."

"Not now, Tully!"

Gus lights the Fluff Bomb. Grey smoke fills the room.

"Free hoodies at the front door!" shouts Vinnie. "Everybody's getting one!"

All the Goldies run to the front. You run out the back with the Creatures.

On the boat, you read the last page of the book. "Biggest net ever. For THE BIG ONE."

Vinnie stares at the sea. "What could need a net that big?"
bands.2:
You have won Slick Vinnie's badge, and Vinnie has never been so happy to lose a sale.

"Captain, you're the only customer who never bought a thing from me," he says. "I respect that. So here's a real deal. Every night at nine, the Vantamart takes a delivery. Tonight, the delivery is you."

Indi has designed the disguises. Everyone will hide in a big cardboard box stamped "LIFE-SIZED MAXX PILLOW". Everyone wears a silver wig and paper teeth.

"We look nothing like pillows," says Tully.

"You look like pillows of Maxx," says Indi. "That's different."

Gus holds up a lumpy grey ball. "The Belly-Button Fluff Bomb. Two years of my own belly-button fluff. That's not gross. That's science."

At nine o'clock, Vinnie wheels the boxes to the back door.

"Fresh stock, gents!" he booms at the Goldies. "Every shop on the planet is ordering these! Can you afford NOT to sign?"

One Goldie signs. The other squints. "Why is that box breathing?"

"Deluxe model," says Vinnie. "Comes with breathing."

Inside, the Vantamart is a canyon of shelves: gold hoodies, Maxx-face pillows and plush hearts that say "SMASH THAT HEART".

At the back is a photo studio. A row of tiny cages is labelled "LIVE MERCH". Inside are Bilbolsters and Proovils, squeezed into tiny gold hoodies. Wren starts on the locks.

Zed types IAMPRICELESS into the office keypad. "That's not a password," he mutters. "That's a cry for help."

Wren walks straight to a dusty grey box labelled "BORING STUFF. DO NOT OPEN."

"He always hides the important things in a boring box," she says. "Lucky guess."

Inside is a gold book: the Rescue Fund ledger. Tully reads it. "Money in, from hoodies: four million dollars. Money spent on Creatures: one carrot. Money spent on a second gold jet ski: everything else."

"Now THAT," says Vinnie, "is a claim with nothing behind it."

You tuck the ledger into your jacket. That's the proof.

Then the lights snap on. Goldies pour in. "Pillows don't have legs!" one yells.

"The Reef Rays just kicked a goal," whispers Tully. "They're only losing by sixty now."

"NOT NOW, Tully!"

Gus lights the Fluff Bomb. Grey smoke billows down the aisles. Vinnie leaps onto a shelf.

"ROLL UP, ROLL UP! Free hoodies at the front door! Everybody's getting one!"

Every Goldie stampedes to the front. You slip out the back with the Creatures.

On the boat, you read the last page of the ledger. "Biggest net ever made. For THE BIG ONE."

Vinnie stops smiling. "I've sold a lot of nets, Captain. Nobody needs one that big. Not for anything that's still swimming out there."
bands.3:
You have won Slick Vinnie's badge, and Slick Vinnie has never been so pleased to lose a sale.

"Captain, you're the only customer in history who has never bought a single thing from me," he says. "I respect that. So here's a real deal. Every night at nine, the Vantamart takes a delivery at the back door. Tonight, the delivery is you."

Indi has designed the disguise of the Chapter. Everyone will hide in a big cardboard box stamped "LIFE-SIZED MAXX PILLOW". Inside, each of you wears a gold tracksuit, a silver wig made of steel wool and paper teeth.

"We look nothing like pillows," says Tully.

"You look exactly like pillows of Maxx," says Indi. "That's different."

Gus pats a lumpy grey ball in his pocket. "The Belly-Button Fluff Bomb," he whispers. "Two years of my own belly-button fluff. Light the fuse, and it makes the thickest smoke you've ever seen. That's not gross. That's science."

At nine o'clock, Vinnie wheels a trolley of boxes up to the back door.

"Evening, gents!" he booms at the two Goldies. "Fresh stock! Every shop on the planet is ordering these. Can you really afford NOT to sign?"

One Goldie signs. The second one squints. "Why is that box breathing?"

"Deluxe model," says Vinnie. "Comes with breathing."

Inside, the Vantamart is a canyon of shelves stacked to the ceiling: gold hoodies, Maxx-face pillows and plush hearts that say "SMASH THAT HEART".

At the very back is a photo studio. In front of a gold backdrop sits a row of tiny cages labelled "LIVE MERCH". Inside are Bilbolsters, Proovils and a cross-looking Squawkle, each one squeezed into a tiny gold hoodie for Maxx's catalogue. A Puffentie in the end cage puffs up in fury and bursts its hoodie at the seams.

"Good," whispers Wren, and starts on the locks.

Next to the studio is an office. Zed tries MAXXISGREAT on the keypad. Wrong. Then he tries IAMPRICELESS, and the door swings open. "That's not a password," he mutters. "That's a cry for help."

Wren walks straight to a dusty grey box labelled "BORING STUFF. DO NOT OPEN. SERIOUSLY, IT'S SO BORING."

"He always hides the important things in a boring box," she says. Everyone looks at her. "Lucky guess."

Inside is a fat gold book: the Rescue Fund ledger. Tully reads it. "Money in, from hoodies: four million dollars. Money spent on Creatures: one carrot. Money spent on a second gold jet ski, 'for Sundays': everything else."

"Now THAT," says Vinnie, "is a claim with nothing holding it up."

You tuck the ledger into your jacket. That's the proof.

Then the lights snap on. Goldies pour in. "Pillows don't have legs!" one of them yells.

"The Reef Rays just kicked a goal," whispers Tully. "They're only losing by sixty now."

"NOT NOW, Tully!"

Gus lights the Fluff Bomb and rolls it down the aisle. Thick grey smoke billows up, smelling faintly of old jumper. Vinnie leaps onto a shelf.

"ROLL UP, ROLL UP! Free gold hoodies at the front door! Everybody's getting one!"

Every Goldie in the building stampedes to the front. You slip out the back, arms full of Creatures, and set them free in the red dust.

Back on the boat, you read the last page of the ledger. One entry is circled twice in gold pen: "Biggest net ever made. Paid for by the Vantafam. For THE BIG ONE."

Vinnie stops smiling. "I've sold a lot of nets, Captain," he says quietly. "Nobody needs one that big. Not for anything that's still swimming in these waters."

He stares out at the dark sea. "Unless something is."
bands.4:
You have won Slick Vinnie's badge, and Slick Vinnie has never been so pleased to lose a sale.

"Captain, you are the only customer in history who has never bought a single thing from me," he says, shaking your hand so hard that your teeth rattle. "I respect that. So here's a deal, and this one is real. Every night at nine, the Vantamart takes a delivery at the back door. The Goldies will sign for anything, as long as it's shiny and the driver is smiling. Tonight, the delivery is you."

Indi has already designed the disguise of the Chapter. Everyone will hide inside a big cardboard box stamped "LIFE-SIZED MAXX PILLOW". Inside the boxes, each of you wears a gold tracksuit, a silver wig made of steel wool and paper teeth painted so white that they hurt to look at.

"We look nothing like pillows," says Tully.

"You look exactly like pillows of Maxx," says Indi. "That's completely different."

Gus pats a lumpy grey ball in his pocket. "The Belly-Button Fluff Bomb," he whispers. "Two whole years of my own belly-button fluff, rolled tight and fitted with a fuse. Light it, and it makes the thickest, fluffiest smoke you've ever seen. That's not gross. That's science."

At nine o'clock, Vinnie wheels a trolley stacked with boxes up to the back door. You're in the second box from the top, and you can hear Zed breathing through his nose.

"Evening, gents!" Vinnie booms at the two Goldies. "Fresh stock! Every shop on the planet is ordering these. Can you really afford NOT to sign?"

The first Goldie signs immediately. The second one squints at the boxes. "Why is that one breathing?"

"Deluxe model," says Vinnie, without missing a beat. "Comes with breathing."

"Koo-koo-ha-ha-HA!" cackles Spruikoo from his shoulder, and the Goldies laugh along as they wave you through.

Inside, the Vantamart is a canyon of shelves stacked to the ceiling with gold hoodies, Maxx-face pillows and plush hearts that say "SMASH THAT HEART". Indi draws a tiny moustache on every Maxx she passes, which turns out to be roughly four thousand Maxxes.

At the very back is a photo studio. In front of a gold backdrop sits a row of tiny cages labelled "LIVE MERCH". Inside are Bilbolsters, Proovils and a cross-looking Squawkle, each one squeezed into a miniature gold hoodie for the catalogue photos. The Puffentie in the end cage hears Zed whisper "rescued", puffs up in fury and bursts its hoodie at the seams.

"Good," whispers Wren, and starts on the locks.

Next to the studio is an office with a gold keypad. Zed tries MAXXISGREAT. Wrong. Then he tries IAMPRICELESS, and the door swings open. "That's not a password," he mutters. "That's a cry for help."

The office is full of filing boxes. Wren walks past every one of them to a dusty grey box on the bottom shelf, labelled "BORING STUFF. DO NOT OPEN. SERIOUSLY, IT'S SO BORING."

"He always hides the important things in a boring box," she says. Everyone looks at her. "Lucky guess."

Inside is a fat gold book: the Rescue Fund ledger. Tully runs her finger down the columns. "Money in, from hoodies: four million dollars," she reads. "Money spent on Creatures: one carrot. Money spent on a second gold jet ski, 'for Sundays': everything else."

"He spent the Rescue Fund on another jet ski," says Gus slowly.

"Now THAT," says Vinnie, "is a claim with absolutely nothing holding it up."

You tuck the ledger inside your jacket. That's the proof.

Then the lights snap on. Goldies pour in from the loading dock. "Pillows don't have legs!" one of them yells.

In Tully's pocket, the footy radio crackles. "The Reef Rays just kicked a goal," she whispers. "They're only losing by sixty now."

"NOT NOW, Tully!"

Gus lights the Fluff Bomb and bowls it down the aisle. Thick grey smoke billows up, smelling faintly of old jumper. In the fog, Vinnie leaps onto a shelf and cups his hands round his mouth.

"ROLL UP, ROLL UP! Free gold hoodies at the front door! Everybody's getting one! Hurry, before they're gone!"

Every Goldie in the building stampedes towards the front door.

You slip out the back with your arms full of Creatures. On the dock, Wren sets them down one by one, and they scamper away into the red dust, still wearing their tiny hoodies.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, you turn to the last page of the ledger. One final entry is circled twice in gold pen: "Biggest net ever made. Paid for by the Vantafam. For THE BIG ONE. Deliver to the Vantadome before the finale."

Vinnie stops smiling. "Friends, I've sold a lot of nets in my time," he says quietly. "Nobody needs one that big. Not for anything that's still swimming in these waters."

He stares out at the dark sea for a long moment.

"Unless," he says, "something is."
